questions.title: Write Greeting File Then Read
questions.description:
Read a name from stdin, write a greeting to a file, then read the file back and print its contents.

Input Format:
Line 1: a name (string).

Output Format:
The exact greeting line written to the file.

Constraints:
Name length 1..30, alphabetic only.
questions.sourcecode:
name = gets.chomp
path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_greet.txt"
File.open(path, "w") { |f| f.puts "Hello, #{name}!" }
puts File.read(path).chomp

questions.title: Read First Line of File
questions.description:
Read three lines of text, write them to a file, then read back only the first line and print it.

Input Format:
Lines 1-3: any non-empty text lines.

Output Format:
The first line written to the file.

Constraints:
Each line length 1..50.

questions.title: Append Line to File
questions.description:
Read a line, truncate a target file (mode w), append the line (mode a), then read the file back and print its contents.

Input Format:
Line 1: any non-empty text.

Output Format:
The appended line.

Constraints:
Line length 1..100.

questions.title: Write Numbers Read Sum
questions.description:
Read an integer n followed by n integers, write each integer on its own line to a file, then read the file back and print the sum of the integers.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: integer values.

Output Format:
The integer sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; -1000 <= value <= 1000.

questions.title: Readlines Count Lines
questions.description:
Read an integer n followed by n lines of text, write them to a file, then read back with `File.readlines` and print the number of lines stored.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: any non-empty text.

Output Format:
The integer count of lines (equal to n).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; each line length 1..80.

questions.title: Create Dir and Glob Files
questions.description:
Read two file basenames (no extension), create a directory if needed, write a single-line .txt file for each name, then count the .txt files inside the directory using `Dir.glob`.

Input Format:
Line 1: two space-separated basenames (alphabetic only).

Output Format:
The integer 2.

Constraints:
Each basename length 1..20, lowercase letters only.
questions.inputconstrains: Each basename length 1..20, lowercase letters only
questions.sourcecode:
names = gets.split
dir = "/tmp/atom_ruby_basic_dir"
Dir.mkdir(dir) unless Dir.exist?(dir)
Dir.glob("#{dir}/*.txt").each { |p| File.delete(p) }
names.each do |name|
  File.open("#{dir}/#{name}.txt", "w") { |f| f.puts "x" }
end
puts Dir.glob("#{dir}/*.txt").size

questions.title: Library Log Appender
questions.description:
A library checkout system appends each book title to a daily log file. Read a book title, write `LOG START` to the file (mode w), then append the title (mode a), and finally read the file back and print the last line.

Input Format:
Line 1: a book title.

Output Format:
The book title line.

Constraints:
Title length 1..100.

questions.title: Coupon Code Tally
questions.description:
A cashier enters coupon codes; valid promotional coupons start with the prefix `SAVE`. Read n coupon codes, write each to a file, then use `File.foreach` to count those starting with `SAVE`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: coupon codes (uppercase letters and digits only).

Output Format:
The count of SAVE-prefixed coupons.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; each code length 1..20.

questions.title: Inventory Snapshot Writer
questions.description:
An inventory clerk records three items (name, quantity, unit price) and saves a formatted receipt file. Read the three items, write each as `name xQTY @ PRICE`, then read the file back and print its full contents.

Input Format:
Lines 1-3: each `name qty price` (whitespace-separated, price has 2 decimals).

Output Format:
Three lines mirroring the file contents.

Constraints:
Name length 1..20; 1 <= qty <= 100; 0.01 <= price <= 1000.00.
questions.sampleoutput1:
apple x5 @ 2.00
banana x3 @ 1.50
cherry x2 @ 4.00
questions.sampleoutput2:
pen x10 @ 1.25
book x2 @ 8.99
lamp x1 @ 15.50
questions.output3:
chair x1 @ 25.00
desk x2 @ 50.00
mat x3 @ 5.00
questions.sourcecode:
items = 3.times.map { gets.split }
path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_receipt.txt"
File.open(path, "w") do |f|
  items.each do |row|
    name, qty, price = row
    f.puts "#{name} x#{qty} @ #{price}"
  end
end
puts File.read(path).chomp

questions.title: Directory Listing Report
questions.description:
A sysadmin wants a listing of the latest log files in a working directory. Read an integer k, create the directory if needed, write `file1.log` through `filek.log` (each containing its index), then list them sorted by name (basename only).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer k.

Output Format:
k lines, each the basename of one log file in sorted order.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 10.

questions.title: Sales Transaction Ledger Reader
questions.description:
A store records daily transactions to a flat file. Read n transactions (each: `product qty price`), write them to a ledger file, then use `File.foreach` to compute total revenue and print `TOTAL: X.XX`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: `product qty price` whitespace-separated.

Output Format:
`TOTAL: X.XX` with 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 1 <= qty <= 100; 0.01 <= price <= 1000.00.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
txns = n.times.map { gets.split }
path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_ledger.txt"
File.open(path, "w") do |f|
  txns.each do |row|
    product, qty, price = row
    f.puts "#{product} #{qty} #{price}"
  end
end
total = 0.0
File.foreach(path) do |line|
  parts = line.split
  total += parts[1].to_i * parts[2].to_f
end
puts "TOTAL: #{"%.2f" % total}"

questions.title: Reverse Lines to Mirror File
questions.description:
A log archiver wants to keep a reversed copy of a log file. Read n lines, write them to a source file, read them back with `File.readlines`, reverse the order, and write the reversed lines to a mirror file. Print the mirror file contents.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: any non-empty text.

Output Format:
n lines, the input lines reversed in order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; each line length 1..80.

questions.title: Append Marker Line Counter
questions.description:
A data pipeline writes n records to a file (mode w), then appends an `END` marker line (mode a). Read the file back (mode r) and print the total number of lines stored.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: any non-empty text records.

Output Format:
The integer n+1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; each record length 1..80.

questions.title: Directory Snapshot Sorted Listing
questions.description:
A release engineer needs a sorted listing of all asset files in a snapshot directory. Read n asset names, create the directory (clearing old .txt files first), write one .txt file per asset (containing its own name), then list basenames sorted alphabetically.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: asset basenames (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
n basenames sorted alphabetically, one per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; each basename length 1..20, lowercase letters only.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50; each basename length 1..20, lowercase letters only

questions.title: File Line and Char Tally
questions.description:
A text-mining tool needs the number of lines and total characters (excluding newlines) in a document. Read n lines, write them to a file, then use `File.foreach` to count lines and characters, printing `LINES: X CHARS: Y`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: any non-empty text.

Output Format:
`LINES: X CHARS: Y` with X=n and Y=total non-newline chars.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; each line length 1..80.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
lines = n.times.map { gets.chomp }
path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_tally.txt"
File.open(path, "w") { |f| lines.each { |l| f.puts l } }
line_count = 0
char_count = 0
File.foreach(path) do |l|
  line_count += 1
  char_count += l.chomp.length
end
puts "LINES: #{line_count} CHARS: #{char_count}"

questions.title: Receipt Append Total Line
questions.description:
A POS system writes itemized receipts then appends a TOTAL line. Read 3 items (each: `name price qty`), write the items to a file (mode w), append `TOTAL X.XX` (mode a), then read back and print all lines.

Input Format:
Lines 1-3: each `name price qty` (whitespace-separated, price has 2 decimals).

Output Format:
Four lines: the three item lines followed by `TOTAL X.XX`.

Constraints:
Name length 1..20; 0.01 <= price <= 1000.00; 1 <= qty <= 100.
questions.sourcecode:
items = 3.times.map { gets.split }
path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_receipt2.txt"
total = 0.0
File.open(path, "w") do |f|
  items.each do |row|
    name, price, qty = row
    f.puts "#{name} #{price} #{qty}"
    total += price.to_f * qty.to_i
  end
end
formatted = "%.2f" % total
File.open(path, "a") { |f| f.puts "TOTAL #{formatted}" }
content = ""
File.open(path, "r") { |f| content = f.read }
puts content.chomp

questions.title: Audit Log Level Summary
questions.description:
An SRE ingests audit log entries and produces a level summary report. Read n log lines (each: `LEVEL message`), write them to a log file, use `File.foreach` to count ERROR/WARN/INFO occurrences, write a summary file (`LEVEL: COUNT` per line), then read the summary back and print it.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: `LEVEL message` (LEVEL is one of ERROR, WARN, INFO).

Output Format:
Three lines: `ERROR: X`, `WARN: Y`, `INFO: Z` (in that fixed order).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; LEVEL is ERROR, WARN, or INFO; message length 1..80.
questions.sampleinput1:
5
ERROR db down
WARN slow query
INFO started
ERROR timeout
INFO done
questions.sampleinput2:
4
INFO boot
INFO ready
WARN low mem
ERROR crash
questions.input1:
3
ERROR a
ERROR b
ERROR c
questions.input3:
5
INFO a
WARN b
ERROR c
INFO d
WARN e
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100; LEVEL is ERROR, WARN, or INFO; message length 1..80

questions.title: Recursive Glob File Counter
questions.description:
A build tool counts note files across nested project directories. Read an integer k, create k subdirectories (sub1..subk) under a k-named root, place one `note.txt` in each subdir, then count all `.txt` files recursively using `Dir.glob` with the `**` pattern.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer k.

Output Format:
The integer k.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 10.
questions.sourcecode:
k = gets.to_i
root = "/tmp/atom_ruby_tree_k#{k}"
Dir.mkdir(root) unless Dir.exist?(root)
1.upto(k) do |i|
  subdir = "#{root}/sub#{i}"
  Dir.mkdir(subdir) unless Dir.exist?(subdir)
  File.open("#{subdir}/note.txt", "w") { |f| f.puts "file #{i}" }
end
files = Dir.glob("#{root}/**/*.txt")
puts files.size

questions.title: Running Balance Append Ledger
questions.description:
A bank teller appends deposit amounts to a ledger file and tracks the running balance. Read n amounts, append each amount to the ledger (mode a, after truncating first), then use `File.foreach` over the ledger to compute running balances and append each to a balances file. Print the final running balance with 2 decimals.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: positive float amounts.

Output Format:
The final running balance formatted to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 0.01 <= amount <= 10000.00.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
amounts = n.times.map { gets.to_f }
ledger = "/tmp/atom_ruby_recon_ledger.txt"
balances = "/tmp/atom_ruby_recon_balances.txt"
File.open(ledger, "w") { |f| }
File.open(balances, "w") { |f| }
amounts.each do |a|
  File.open(ledger, "a") { |f| f.puts a }
end
running = 0.0
File.foreach(ledger) do |line|
  running += line.to_f
  File.open(balances, "a") { |f| f.puts "%.2f" % running }
end
final = 0.0
File.foreach(balances) do |line|
  final = line.to_f
end
puts "%.2f" % final

questions.title: Catalog CSV to Summary File
questions.description:
A shop exports its catalog as a CSV-like file and wants a summary report. Read n rows (each: `sku,name,price`), write each to a catalog file, read back with `File.readlines` (parsing CSV manually by splitting on commas — do NOT use the CSV library), compute the count and total price, write `COUNT n` and `TOTAL X.XX` lines to a summary file, append an `END` marker, then read back and print the summary.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: `sku,name,price` (price has 2 decimals).

Output Format:
Three lines: `COUNT n`, `TOTAL X.XX`, `END`.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; sku length 1..10; name length 1..20; 0.01 <= price <= 1000.00.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100; sku length 1..10; name length 1..20; 0.01 <= price <= 1000.00
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
rows = n.times.map { gets.chomp }
catalog_path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_catalog.txt"
File.open(catalog_path, "w") { |f| rows.each { |r| f.puts r } }
total = 0.0
count = 0
File.readlines(catalog_path).each do |line|
  parts = line.chomp.split(",")
  total += parts[2].to_f
  count += 1
end
summary_path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_catalog_summary.txt"
File.open(summary_path, "w") do |f|
  f.puts "COUNT #{count}"
  f.puts "TOTAL #{"%.2f" % total}"
end
File.open(summary_path, "a") { |f| f.puts "END" }
content = ""
File.open(summary_path, "r") { |f| content = f.read }
puts content.chomp
